Sharp tax work. An accounting brain. A soft spot for better systems.

Job postings are funny

They are often part wish list, part sales pitch, and part collection of phrases no human has ever used in conversation. That does not tell you what the work feels like, who you will work with, or whether you will actually enjoy being here. We would rather be honest, so here is the real story.

About PracticeDen and R.D. Barnett PLLC

PracticeDen grew out of R.D. Barnett PLLC, the tax, accounting, and advisory firm Dean Barnett founded to help entrepreneurs and privately held businesses make smarter financial decisions. Years of sitting beside business owners - not just filing returns for them - made one thing clear: independent veterinary practice owners deserved an advisor who understood both the numbers and the wonderfully complicated business behind them.

That is where PracticeDen comes in. We connect the entire financial picture, from the operating practice and related real estate to the owner's individual tax situation. We work with veterinary owners as they start, buy, operate, grow, and eventually transition their practices. The goal is bigger than accurate filings. We want our clients to understand their numbers, spot opportunities earlier, make confident decisions, and spend less time wondering what their accountant is talking about.

PracticeDen is the veterinary-focused brand of R.D. Barnett PLLC. It is not a separate firm or a tax-only team. This role has a functional home in Tax and works across PracticeDen with accounting, advisory, and client-service teammates so the practice, related real estate, and owner return tell one coherent story.

The Role (and Why It's Interesting)

We are looking for an experienced, hard-working, and self-motivated Senior Tax Associate who can prepare a wide variety of returns, hand off thoughtful, reviewer-ready work, and help us make tax season run a little smarter. You will work across entity and individual clients, often following the numbers across a veterinary practice, related real estate, and the owner's personal return.

This role reports to Liz Sandstrom, EA, Tax Manager. Liz leads the tax side of PracticeDen and will be your primary coach, reviewer, supervisor, and escalation point. You will own day-to-day execution, workpaper quality, status visibility, and early issue identification. Liz will set technical direction, approve material positions, and help you grow toward greater independence, planning exposure, client leadership, and review responsibility.

Tax preparation is the main event. You will gather information, build workpapers, prepare calculations and returns, support planning, handle e-filing and delivery, research unusual issues, and help resolve notices or other technical projects. In other words: you will do real tax work from beginning to end, not spend your days moving numbers from one box to another without understanding why.

This is also not a stay-in-your-lane-forever role. While traditional accounting work won’t be your primary responsibility, a strong accounting brain is essential. You should be able to read a trial balance, understand the financial statements, reconcile important accounts, propose adjustments, and recognize when the accounting needs attention before a return can move forward. Recurring bookkeeping is not part of this role unless separately assigned and scoped.

As PracticeDen grows, this role can grow with it. We do not expect you to know every answer. We do expect you to be genuinely inquisitive with a solution-driven purpose: ask better questions, trace the issue to its source, and move toward a sensible answer. Prior veterinary-industry experience is welcome but not required. Curiosity about independent veterinary ownership is.

What You'll Actually Do

Make tax work look easy

  • Prepare the returns. All kinds of them. That includes federal, state, and local returns for individuals and closely held entities, with a core mix of Forms 1040, 1065, 1120-S, and 1120. It may also include trusts and estates, related real estate entities, and other returns as assigned.
  • Make review a pleasant experience. Build clean, complete workpapers with clear support, reconciliations, calculations, notes, and tie-outs. Your reviewer should not need detective training to follow your work.
  • Follow the financial trail. Connect practice, real estate, and individual filings so every related return tells the same story.
  • Bring an accounting brain to the return. Reconcile balance-sheet accounts, retained earnings, fixed assets, basis, owner activity, payroll, sales or excise tax, and other book-to-tax items that are part of the engagement.
  • Know what went into the software. Enter and validate tax data, carryforwards, fixed assets, prior-year items, and current-year activity in UltraTax CS or a comparable platform.
  • Raise your hand early. Spot missing information, inconsistencies, unusual issues, capacity concerns, and potential deadline problems before they become deadline-day surprises.
  • See the process through. Help with extensions, estimates, e-filing, secure delivery, tax notices, and the less-glamorous details that still have to be right.
  • Know when the work has changed. Recognize services outside the agreed scope and bring them to Liz before committing to additional work, fees, or timing.
  • Support planning without freelancing. Identify potential planning opportunities, research assigned questions, document the facts and authority, and bring clear recommendations and unresolved questions to Liz.

Use technology like you mean it

  • Make Excel earn its keep. Build traceable workpapers and useful analyses, clean up data, review trial balances, and propose journal entries without turning the workbook into a haunted house.
  • Pick up new tools quickly. Tax software, workflow platforms, portals, collaboration tools-if it makes the work better, you should be comfortable learning it.
  • Use AI thoughtfully, not blindly. Look for responsible ways to improve research, documentation, data handling, and repetitive workflows. Use only firm-approved systems, protect client information, verify every output, and remain accountable for the final work.
  • Notice when a process is clunky, then improve it. Test practical fixes, document what works, and help us scale without trading accuracy for speed.

Be a great human to work with

  • Keep people out of the dark. Communicate about status, open items, scope, risks, and deadlines before someone has to chase you.
  • Write like a person. Draft clear, professional client emails and explain requests without burying the point in tax jargon.
  • Treat review notes as fuel. Ask thoughtful questions, apply the feedback, and make the next engagement better.
  • Help shape the Den. Contribute to documentation, training, and the systems and habits our growing team will rely on.
  • Work across the team. Coordinate with accounting, advisory, and client-service teammates when the tax return exposes an accounting issue, planning opportunity, or client need.

What You Bring to the Den

The must-haves

  • Real tax experience. You have at least three years of recent public accounting tax experience, including at least two busy seasons owning returns from client intake through reviewer submission. You can prepare a varied return mix, understand what the numbers mean, and deliver work that is truly ready for review.
  • Individual and entity experience. You have meaningful experience with individual and closely held business returns, not just one narrow slice of a return.
  • A strong accounting brain. You can read financial statements, reconcile accounts, understand journal entries, and trace activity into a tax return without losing the plot.
  • Excel power-user energy. Formulas, lookups, pivot tables, data cleanup, and well-organized workpapers should feel familiar, not frightening.
  • An eye for the tiny things. You catch the transposed number, the missing support, and the line that does not tie before someone else does.
  • AI and automation curiosity. When you see a repetitive process, you naturally wonder whether a robot should be doing the boring part. You are excited to test better ways of working, but you do not hand the robot the keys and walk away. Approved tools, client privacy, professional judgment, and verified outputs are nonnegotiable.
  • Clear communication and sound judgment. You write well, think before you act, and can receive feedback without turning it into a courtroom drama.
  • Busy-season stamina. You are prepared for 55+ hours during the heaviest filing-deadline stretches, typically February through April 15 and September through October 15. We hope that is reserved for the worst of times, not the regular rhythm. Busy season should be a season, not a year-round personality.
  • Remote-work reliability. You maintain a secure, professional workspace, dependable internet, and availability for Pacific Time collaboration during agreed working hours.
  • Professional references from prior employers, supervisors, or clients.

CPA or Enrolled Agent credential is not required. We value demonstrated capability, sound judgment, and a commitment to continued learning.

Bonus points for:

  • CPA license, EA certification, CPA eligibility, or active progress toward a credential
  • Experience reviewing simpler returns or training less-experienced preparers
  • Tax-tech fluency with UltraTax CS or another professional preparation platform, e-file and portal workflows, or digital delivery tools
  • A useful AI or automation story: something you improved, sped up, or made less painful in a tax or accounting workflow
  • Comfort around the broader accounting stack, such as QuickBooks, Workpapers CS, Practice CS, SurePrep, SafeSend, SharePoint, Notion, Missive, , Gusto, Double, or similar systems
  • Experience with wonderfully complicated owners: closely held businesses, multi-entity structures, real estate, professional practices, or veterinary-industry clients
  • Multistate, pass-through entity tax, basis, fixed asset, owner compensation, or closely held business planning experience

You'll probably thrive here if...

  • You keep the details on a short leash. Projects, files, open questions, and deadlines do not mysteriously disappear on your watch.
  • You communicate before people have to ask. A clear update today is better than a heroic explanation tomorrow.
  • You care about service. You want clients and teammates to have a genuinely good experience, and you are willing to take out the trash - literally or figuratively - when that is what helps.
  • You can be trusted. You use discretion, exercise good judgment, and protect sensitive client information as if it were your own.
  • You are genuinely inquisitive with a solution-driven purpose. You ask why, research and test what you do not know, and turn curiosity into a practical next step instead of collecting interesting questions for sport.
  • You own your work. Mistakes happen; hiding them or repeating them is the problem. You speak up, fix the issue, and learn from it.
  • You can handle change. PracticeDen is growing, technology keeps moving, and the perfect process may not exist yet.
  • You take the work seriously without taking yourself too seriously. Public accounting is demanding. A sense of humor makes the hard days better.
  • You build momentum as a form of mutual appreciation. You follow through, communicate early, and move work forward because making teammates chase you is nobody's love language.

How You'll Know You're Crushing It

  • Your reviewer can follow your work without a scavenger hunt. Returns tie, support is clear, and avoidable review notes become rare.
  • There are fewer surprises. Missing information, odd activity, planning ideas, scope changes, and potential problems surface early.
  • People trust your follow-through. Client requests make sense, deadlines stay visible, and projects do not vanish into a status-update black hole.
  • The systems get smarter. You adopt new tools thoughtfully and improve processes without weakening accuracy, controls, or confidentiality.
  • The numbers work too. You meet the production, realization, timekeeping, and project-delivery expectations assigned to your role and portfolio.
  • You get better every cycle. Feedback shows up in the next engagement, and your confidence, judgment, and independence keep growing.

The Practical Stuff: Pay, Benefits, and Where You'll Work

Now, let's talk about the part of the job everyone scrolls for.

  • Compensation: Full-time, exempt position with a base salary of $80,000-$105,000 annually, depending on experience, credentials, and demonstrated capability.
  • Flexible start: The position may begin as early as September 22, 2026 or as late as January 4, 2027.
  • Remote work: This is a remote position within U.S. states and localities approved by the firm. Changes in primary work location or regular work from another state or locality require advance approval.
  • Working hours: The role must maintain dependable availability for Pacific Time collaboration, client needs, training, and scheduled team meetings. The heaviest filing-deadline stretches may require 55+ hours, but that should describe the worst of times, not most of the time.
  • Travel: Travel may be requested for quarterly all-hands firm meetings and occasional destination continuing professional education. The firm will fully reimburse approved business travel in accordance with firm travel and expense policies.
  • Equipment: The firm provides the computer and standard technology equipment needed for the role, including monitors, keyboard, mouse, headset, and related accessories.
  • Medical, dental, and vision: The firm currently pays 100% of the employee premium for its medical plan (BCBS PPO) and dental and vision plans (Delta Dental PPO). Coverage begins on the first day of the month following the employee's start date. Dependents may be added at the employee's cost. Benefits remain subject to plan terms.
  • 401(k): The firm currently matches employee contributions up to 3% of eligible pay. Eligibility begins on the employee's start date, subject to plan terms and the applicable vesting schedule.
  • Paid holidays: Six current firm holidays - New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Thanksgiving Day, the day after Thanksgiving, and Christmas Day - plus four floating holidays. Tax-season blackout dates apply.
  • Vacation: Fifteen vacation days per calendar year, prorated based on the official start date. Vacation is subject to the firm calendar and busy-season blackout periods.
  • Paid sick and safe time: Accrual begins on the first day of employment. The firm uses Seattle's paid sick and safe time requirements as its minimum standard and applies any more protective law required by the employee's work location.
  • Volunteer time: Two paid volunteer days.
  • Professional development: Continuing education and growth opportunities, including reimbursement for approved certification, licensing, professional membership, and destination CPE expenses within firm policy.
  • Optional cell-phone coverage: Participation in the firm's Verizon plan is available under the current cell-phone policy. The firm does not subsidize or reimburse the purchase of the device.
  • Personal tax support: Employees may use firm software to prepare their personal income tax returns and may request reasonable tax guidance from the firm's principals at no charge, subject to firm policy.

Ready to Join the Den?

If you are a strong tax preparer with an accounting mind, a sharp eye, and genuine curiosity about better technology, we would love to hear from you. Bring your judgment, your Excel shortcuts, and your best ideas for making tax work better. We will bring interesting clients, meaningful work, and a team that cares about doing both well!

Come join us in the Den.

How to Apply and How to Stand Out

Apply through the official job posting once it is live. We will consider complete applications in the following order:

  1. Introductory video: Candidates who submit a thoughtful 30-second to 3-minute introductory video will move to the top of the review list. Tell us who you are, why the role caught your attention, and what you would bring to PracticeDen. Production quality is not the point. We want to meet the human behind the resume.
  2. Thoughtful cover letter: Candidates who write a specific, genuine cover letter will be considered next.
  3. Standard application: We will also consider candidates who submit the application without a video or cover letter.

We notice thoughtful follow-up. A respectful LinkedIn message or direct email to a member of our team after applying can help us understand your interest and how you communicate. Please keep it human, specific, and concise.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

R.D. Barnett PLLC is an equal opportunity employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, citizenship or immigration status, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital status, disability, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the hiring process. Applicants who require an accommodation may contact .

raw.excerpt: About WillfulWillful makes estate planning easy, affordable, and accessible for every Canadian.
raw.description:
About Willful

Willful makes estate planning easy, affordable, and accessible for every Canadian. Since 2017, over 400,000 people have trusted us to help them build their legal estate documents.

Partnerships are a vital driver of Willful’s growth engine. They help us open doors to new audiences, collaborate with brands our customers trust, and are a meaningful revenue stream for Willful. Equally important, we create lasting, measurable value alongside our partners.

By teaming up with Willful, partners can expand their offer with a trusted, modern estate planning solution that seamlessly deepens customer engagement, unlocks new revenue opportunities, and solves a real, high-priority need for their audience. Together, we create win-win relationships that drive real impact for both of our businesses and the Canadians we serve.

The Role

We're looking for an organized and proactive Partnerships Coordinator who can tackle projects from brief to final delivery while keeping a lot of moving pieces on track. This is a hands-on, execution role at the heart of our partnerships team.

The ideal candidate is someone motivated by output: building campaign assets, running and improving partner operations, holding timelines and stakeholders on track, supporting inbound advisor calls, and turning performance data into clear reporting. This is an operational and supporting role. You'll be the internal engine that keeps our partnerships running day to day.

To thrive in Willful’s remote-first environment on a small, agile, two-person partnerships team, you will need to be resourceful, proactive, curious, have a bias to action, and be open to direct, clear feedback. If you are someone who requires a lot of continuous oversight, or who needs work to be assigned before you act, this may not be the ideal environment for you.

What You’ll Do

1. Partnership Operations & Advisor Sales

  • Run operations smoothly, from order processing and month-end reconciliations to invoicing, briefs, and follow-ups.
  • Build repeatable scalable workflows, keep documentation up to date, and automate routine tasks using AI and modern software tools.
  • Create professional partner decks, one-pagers, and clear performance updates.
  • Support our Willful for Professionals platform for financial advisors, including supporting with inbound sales materials and meetings

2. Campaign Execution & Asset Creation

  • Design and produce campaign assets across multiple mediums, including static graphics, short-form video, co-branded emails, and social channels.
  • Ship campaigns on time while keeping internal parties informed, aligned, and accountable.
  • Bring fresh, practical creative ideas to the table for new partner activations.

3. Performance & Impact

  • Track partner-sourced revenue and transaction volume.
  • Build and refine reporting across all partnership channels.
  • Share honest, straightforward updates on what is working and what isn'

Who You Are

  • A natural doer and builder: You have a track record of executing projects in an agency, startup, freelance, or fast-paced environment.
  • Proactive and fast on your feet: You do not wait for a playbook. You take a brief, ask questions and run with it.
  • A multi-medium creator: You have design and asset creation skills, including basic video editing, and know your way around Figma and Notion.
  • AI-savvy: You actively use AI tools in your workflow to work smarter and ship faster.
  • Open to rapid iteration: You take direct feedback in stride and enjoy refining your work until it shines.
  • Problem-Solving Focused: You identify and step in to improve systems with solutions without being asked.
  • A Natural Collaborator: You proactively bridge gaps between teams to solve problems and make work easier for everyone.
  • Data-literate and articulate: You can write clearly, know how to represent a brand well to external partners, and know how to analyze and share relevant metrics internally and externally.

Bonus Points

  • Bilingual in French and English (written and verbal).
  • 1 to 3 years in marketing, sales, partnerships, or project coordination.
  • Experience running sales, business development, or discovery calls.
  • Video editing expertise.
  • Background working in/with trust-based industries like finance, law, or health.

Perks & Benefits

  • Salary: $50,000 to $60,000 CAD (commensurate with experience).
  • Equity: Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) participation.
  • Health & Wellness: Full health, dental, and vision coverage, plus a $500 annual wellness budget.
  • Flexible Perks: Your choice between a Health Spending Account (HSA) or RRSP matching.
  • Flexible work: A 4.5-day work week year-round, flexible working hours, and company-wide paid 'recharge' days in December on top of standard vacation.
  • Team Culture: Monthly meal and entertainment budget, fun virtual events, and an in-person team retreat once a year.

How We Hire

  1. Initial Screen: 30-minute chat with the Partnerships Manager.
  2. Workshop: A practical live session to see how we work together.
  3. Final Round: 30-minute interview with the Partnerships Manager and Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder.
  4. Culture Q&A: 30-minute chat with the Senior Operations Manager to learn about Willful’s culture, values, and working environment.
  5. References & Offer

Work where you want to

We’re looking for the right person to join our team so this role isn’t limited by geography and will be 100% remote. The only requirement is that you must be legally able to work in Canada.

Ready to Apply?

If you are ready to help Canadians navigate important life decisions with clarity, send us:

  • A brief note on why Willful stands out to you and how your background fits this role.
  • A quick overview of a project or campaign you owned from start to finish. Tell us what worked, what did not, and share links to any work samples or side projects you are proud of.

We’re building a diverse team

Willful is committed to building a diverse team and encourages applications from individuals from underrepresented groups, including but not limited to women, racialized individuals, Indigenous people, 2SLGBTQIA+ individuals, and persons with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request throughout the hiring process.

AI Disclosure Statement

Willful uses artificial intelligence tools for internal note-taking purposes only. These tools do not influence candidate screening, evaluation, or hiring decisions, and are used solely to support accurate documentation and efficient internal communication.

Salary: $50,000 – $60,000 / year

Join us at MMS and be part of a team that is shaping the future of clinical research.

Discover more about our exciting opportunities and why MMS is a great place to advance your career. Visit or follow MMS on LinkedIn.

We are looking for a full-time employee, remotely based within Argentina.

Responsibilities

  • Under minimal supervision, the Medical Writer will critically evaluate, analyze, and interpret the medical literature to select primary resource materials for adequate study design, statistical significance, scientific rigor and absence of bias
  • Write and edit clinical development documents, including but not limited to, clinical protocols, investigator’s brochures, clinical study reports, subject consent forms, integrated safety and efficacy summaries, Module 2.7.1, 2.7.2, 2.7.3, 2.7.4, and 2.5 documents, presentation materials and publications to medical journals.

  • Interact directly and independently with client to coordinate all facets of projects; competent communicator skills for projects.

  • Mentor medical writers and other members of the project team who are involved in the writing process.

Requirements

  • At least 3 years of previous experience in the pharmaceutical industry.
  • Must have at least 3-5 years of industry regulatory writing and clinical medical writing experience.
  • The ideal candidate would hold a Bachelors, Masters, or Ph.D. in scientific, medical, clinical discipline.
  • Substantial clinical study protocol experience, as lead author, required.
  • Experience leading and managing teams while authoring regulatory documents with aggressive timelines.
  • Experience in regulatory submissions (clinical study reports) presented to regulatory authorities a plus.
  • Understanding of clinical data.
  • Exceptional writing skills are a must.
  • Excellent organizational skills and the ability to multi-task are essential prerequisites.
  • Candidate must be an expert in MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and related word processing tools.
  • Experience being a project lead, or managing a project team.
  • Strong understanding of federal regulations, Good Clinical Practices, and ICH guidelines a plus.
  • Substantial clinical study protocol experience, as lead author, required.
  • Experience leading and managing teams while authoring regulatory documents with aggressive timelines.
  • Not required, but experience with orphan drug designations and PSP/PIPs a plus.

MovieWeb is a top destination for fans of television and movies, providing engaging and informative coverage of the entertainment industry.

We're looking for writers who are passionate about movies, television, and streaming content, with a strong understanding of what audiences are watching right now.

Successful candidates will be able to identify emerging trends, attend advance theatrical screenings and watch digital screenings in advance to develop engaging feature ideas that resonate with readers. They should be comfortable working within an SEO-driven environment, conducting research, and crafting compelling articles that balance search intent with editorial quality. The ideal writer is proactive, creative, and capable of consistently pitching and producing timely content that drives readership and engagement.

Your Responsibilities

  • Write daily feature articles focused on newly released movies and TV shows or trends with editorial support
  • Have a functional understanding of New Release ideation
  • Attend screenings to identify and pitch timely, trend-driven content ideas related to recent releases and audience interests
  • Analyze entertainment trends, streaming performance, social media conversations, and audience engagement patterns
  • Conduct research to produce informative, accurate, and engaging content
  • Apply SEO best practices to maximize discoverability and readership
  • Comfortable meeting deadlines
  • Ensure timely publication of relevant content aligned with SEO and engagement goals
  • Follow guidelines rigorously

What We Offer

  • Fully remote
  • Opportunities to pitch original ideas
  • An amazing community of like-minded people to nerd-out with on a daily basis

Experience and Skills

  • At least 3 years experience in digital journalism or online publishing
  • Strong feature writing and storytelling abilities
  • Ability to identify trends and develop compelling article concepts independently
  • Solid understanding of movies, television, streaming platforms, and current pop culture trends
  • Familiarity with SEO principles, keyword research, and content optimization
  • Experience using CMS platforms and digital publishing tools
  • Excellent research skills and attention to detail

This is a performance-driven freelance position focused on quality, traffic performance, and reliability.

How to Apply

If you are interested in this role, please send us the following documentation by uploading it in the relevant fields below:

  • Your CV
  • 2 sample feature articles (can be links or PDFs)

Our hiring team will review your application and contact you if we believe that your experience could be a match for this role.

Please note that a writing evaluation may be required as part of our application process.

MovieWeb is part of the Valnet Publishing Group.

Valnet, founded in 2012, is a global digital publishing and media investment Company that owns and operates over 27 authoritative brands across diverse verticals, including entertainment, sports, technology, automotive, gaming, lifestyle and travel.

Valnet is committed to producing premium content, and we therefore require all our contributors to adhere to our Editorial Standards, including a prohibition on using Artificial Intelligence.

Financial Coach (Independent Contractor – 1099)

Help Create a Wealth Revolution

Tardus Wealth Strategies is a fast-growing national wealth coaching company on a mission to create a Wealth Revolution.

For more than 20 years, we've helped individuals and families build lasting financial success through education, accountability, and proven wealth-building strategies. Our Wealth Coaches guide clients through our patented Income Snowball™ System and proprietary Six Pillars of Wealth™, helping them create sustainable habits and achieve meaningful financial progress.

We're looking for influential, approachable, and growth-minded coaches who are passionate about changing lives. If you enjoy building long-term relationships, inspiring action, and helping people succeed, we'd love to meet you.

What You'll Do

As a Tardus Wealth Coach, you'll serve as a trusted guide, helping clients confidently implement our proven system and stay accountable to their goals.

You'll:

  • Coach clients through the Income Snowball™ System Six Pillars of Wealth™.
  • Conduct engaging coaching sessions that educate, encourage, and inspire action.
  • Help clients overcome obstacles, celebrate progress, and stay committed to their financial goals.
  • Build long-term client relationships that lead to exceptional results and high renewal rates.
  • Follow established coaching systems while continually developing your own skills.

Our Six Pillars of Wealth™ include:

  • Pillar 1: the Income Snowball™
  • Pillar 2: Risk Alignment
  • Pillar 3: Investment Criteria
  • Pillar 4: Due Diligence
  • Pillar 5: Contingency Planning
  • Pillar 6: Team Alignment

Comprehensive training is provided on our coaching framework and systems.

Who You Are

You're someone who:

  • Enjoys helping people succeed.
  • Builds trust naturally and communicates with confidence and empathy.
  • Listens well and asks thoughtful questions.
  • Is organized, dependable, and coachable.
  • Learns systems quickly and follows proven processes.
  • Thrives independently while contributing to a collaborative team.
  • Is committed to continuous growth and personal development.

Compensation & Perks

  • Monthly coaching fees plus recurring residual commissions.
  • Six-figure income potential.
  • Flexible, fully remote schedule.
  • Comprehensive onboarding and ongoing coaching development.
  • Leadership and personal growth training.
  • Opportunity to build long-term recurring income while making a meaningful impact.

Our Core Values

We hire for character as much as capability.

  • Trust
  • Excellence over Perfection
  • Accountability
  • Collaboration
  • Service
  • Innovation
  • Gratitude

Is This Role Right for You?

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys helping others, embraces accountability, adapts quickly, communicates well, and thrives in a fast-paced, purpose-driven environment.

Why Tardus?

For over 20 years, Tardus has helped families improve their financial future through education, coaching, and innovative wealth-building strategies.

Our coaches don't simply provide information—they build lasting relationships, guide clients through a proven system, and help transform lives while building a rewarding recurring income.

If you're ready to make a meaningful impact while growing your own success, we'd love to hear from you.

Vice President, Business Development


HRforGrowth® is engaged as the talent acquisition partner to conduct this search on behalf of a client organization that is hiring for this role. HRforGrowth is not the employer for this position. HRforGrowth identifies, evaluates, and presents top-tier candidates through its global talent acquisition practice; all employment decisions — including final selection, offer terms, compensation, and conditions of employment — are made solely by the hiring organization.

Role Summary
The Vice President of Business Development “VPBD" is a strategic lead role responsible for driving the company's profitable revenue growth through consultative solution selling, resulting in a gain in market share. This individual will hunt for new business and engage directly with clients’ multi-level stakeholders to understand their business needs and then sell “custom fit” solutions of high financial value that address their requirements. The VPBD will play a crucial role in leading our company growth by ensuring we solve high financial value problems for clients and enhancing client relationships, so they become our avid advocates – all resulting in meeting or exceeding our revenue and profit targets.

This position operates as a crucial individual contributor to business growth as a member of the Business Development team, fostering close working relationships with clients and internal/external stakeholders to ensure success. The VPBD will be responsible for modeling company values and promoting the company culture.

Key Result Areas

“Hunting” / Consultative Selling
  • Compete to win constantly and consistently.
  • Identify and target potential clients through research, networking, and outreach activities.
  • Develop and maintain a robust pipeline of qualified leads.
  • Use various channels, including cold calling, email campaigns, social media, and industry events, to generate new business opportunities. Marketing will provide support.
  • Effectively utilize “pitch” scripts to consistently increase sales conversion rates.  
  • Conduct thorough needs assessments to understand the client’s business challenges, processes, and outsourcing requirements. Provide “custom fit” solutions.
  • Prepare and deliver compelling sales presentations with financials, proposals, value propositions, and contracts.
  • Stay informed, with support from Marketing, about industry trends, competitive landscape, and emerging technologies to continuously refine the sales approach.
  • Represent the company at industry events, conferences, and client meetings to promote solutions offerings.
  • Set the example of a Professional Sales Leader, demonstrating a high “bias for action,” success in “hunting” for and closing sales. Champion the company’s guiding principles and values.

Negotiation and Closing
  • Lead negotiations with prospective clients to finalize contracts and agreements.
  • Collaborate with Pricing, Legal, and other teams to facilitate deal wins.
  • Understand contractual terms and requirements as well as commercial terms to ensure profitability.  
  • Address any objections or concerns raised by clients during the sales process.
  • Close deals promptly while ensuring that all terms are mutually beneficial.

Client Engagement and Account Growth
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key decision-makers and stakeholders at prospective client organizations.
  • Conduct ongoing research of the client’s business and stay abreast with changes in their space. Maintain a Key Account Plan (KAP) for each client
  • Act as the primary point of contact for clients during the sales process, ensuring a smooth and positive experience.
  • Coordinate innovation sessions/events with clients including, but not limited to, Joint Solving, Product Knowledge training, public relations events, and consumer-facing activities.
  • Continuously engage to identify opportunities for upselling or expanding services. Coordinate Monthly and Quarterly business reviews. Support Client Satisfaction Surveys and related improvements.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Innovation
  • Work closely with the internal teams to develop customized solutions that deliver measurable value to clients.
  • Partner with marketing, product development, and customer success teams to align sales strategies with product offerings and customer experiences.
  • Provide feedback to product teams based on customer insights and market trends to inform future product development.
  • Collaborate with Solutions Engineering, Finance, Operations, Technology, and other internal groups to ensure teams have the necessary resources and support to achieve goals on time as promised to clients.

CRM Management
  • Fully utilize CRM system to help maximize personal sales and support the overall Pro Sales team’s results.
  • Provide ongoing updates through CRM, including revenue and profitability (Contribution Margin) projections for new and existing Clients in assigned portfolios.
  • Drive and track opportunity pipeline growth and measure sales effectiveness and conversion rates.

Requirements
  • Degree in Business, Marketing, Technology, or a related field considered a plus.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in business development using consultative solutions sales within the CX and BPO industries.
  • A “Closer” able to develop relationships with C-Level, VP, and the key CX executives and teams to close new sales, grow share of wallet in existing partnerships, and successfully solicit referral business from your network.
  • Proven track record in selling complex solutions (multi-buyer/multi-step) at the executive level in medium to large sectors, as well as Fortune 500 organizations
  • Successful at closing transactions over $5M
  • Deep understanding of the CX/Call Center industry, end to end to include a strong knowledge of financial modeling in an outsourced environment, combined with “outsourcing solutions” sales experience.
  • Demonstrated expert-level skills using Microsoft PowerPoint for Value Proposition and Excel for Financials
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills
  • Strong analytical and strategic thinking skills, with intense attention to detail
  • Have successfully worked in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, possessing a “start-up” mentality, with a high bias for action, agility, and an ability to work independently toward the common goal
  • Willing and able to travel as needed to meet clients, and partners and attend industry events




About HRforGrowth:
HRforGrowth is a full-service HR and talent partner built to support companies that are scaling, transforming, or navigating change. HRFG is globally recognized for delivering quality, speed, and cost-effective talent solutions across every level of the workforce. Through its global talent acquisition practice, HRforGrowth applies world class rigor and precision to identifying exceptional professional and executive talent on behalf of its clients — from temporary staffing to permanent hourly workers through to placing C-suite executives. HRforGrowth is presenting this opportunity in its capacity as the retained search partner and does not serve as the employer of record for this position.

Equal Employment Opportunity:
In its recruiting and search practices, HRforGrowth does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender, or gender identity, and welcomes applications from all qualified individuals. HRforGrowth evaluates and presents candidates to its clients without regard to any protected characteristic.

HRforGrowth endeavors to advise the hiring organization to comply with all applicable federal, state, and local equal employment opportunity laws — including those enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) — in its hiring decisions, terms of employment, and workplace practices.

Reports To: Executive Director

Status: FTE 0.8 - 4 days per week

Direct Reports: ● Finance Coordinator

● Administration Coordinator
● Grants and Finance Officer
Location: Remote working, based in Australia, Germany, the Netherlands, or the United Kingdom.
You must have the right to work in the country for which you apply. IDC is unable to support work visa applications or relocation.
Languages: Fluency and excellent communication skills in oral and written English
Compensation: Per annum depending on skills and experience:
Australia - SCHADS Level 6, pro rata for 0.8 FTE
The Netherlands, Germany, UK - 48,000-56,000 EUR gross annually for 0.8 FTE (based on a full-time equivalent of 60,000-70,000 EUR)

Background

International Detention Coalition (IDC) is a unique global network of over 200 civil society organisations and individuals in more than 75 countries, which coordinates with members and partners on advocacy, research, coalition and capacity building, to eliminate immigration detention and advance rights-based alternatives to detention. IDC is a highly recognised, impact-driven organisation, offering a stimulating workplace committed to local, national, regional and global change.

Role Purpose

The Operations Manager is responsible for making sure the organisation has the financial, legal, human resources (HR) systems, and operational infrastructure needed to function effectively, and sustainably, including risk management and ensuring compliance in the countries where IDC operates.

Role Summary

The Operations Manager provides strategic leadership for the organisation's financial, legal, HR systems, and operational infrastructure, ensuring that the organisation has the systems, capacity and controls required to operate effectively, sustainably and compliantly in multi-currency and multi-country settings.

The role sets the frameworks, standards and priorities through which operational functions are delivered, providing oversight of the Finance Coordinator, Administration Coordinator and Grants and Finance Officer, as well as relevant external providers. The Operations Manager focuses on organisational systems, planning, risk, quality and improvement.

The role is responsible for strengthening the organisation's operational infrastructure as it develops, ensuring that systems are fit for purpose, risks are identified and appropriately managed, legal and regulatory obligations are met, and personnel have the systems and support they need to work effectively.

The Operations Manager reports to the Executive Director (ED) and works closely with the Programmes Manager, Finance and Administration personnel, Regional Managers, and relevant service providers. The Operations Manager forms part of the Senior Management Team.

Role Responsibilities

Finance and Organisational Sustainability

  • Provide strategic oversight of financial management, grants financial management, budgeting, forecasting and organisational finances.
  • Oversee and support the Finance Coordinator and Grants and Finance Officer, ensuring effective implementation of finance and grants systems.
  • Work closely with the ED, Programmes Manager, finance and admin team, and relevant managers on annual budgeting and financial planning.
  • Ensure effective monitoring of financial performance, cash flow, expenditure and financial risks, providing advice to the ED and Senior Management Team.
  • Oversee the establishment and management of appropriate financial controls, payrolls systems, approval processes and delegations.
  • Oversee relationships with accountants, auditors, tax advisers and other financial service providers.
  • Lead on the improvements to financial systems as the organisation develops or operates in new places.
  • Oversee budgeting systems and allocations ensuring accurate compliance of grants finance and audit requirements.
  • Work closely with the Finance Coordinator and oversee the annual audit processes for IDC and other related programme audits.
  • Ensure financial systems provide accurate and timely information for informed organisational decision-making.

Human Resources Systems

  • Support the Executive Director to implement the organisation's human resources systems, ensuring personnel structures and capabilities are aligned with organisational priorities and needs.
  • Develop and implement recruitment and planning strategies and systems, including approaches to attracting, retaining and developing personnel across different regions and jurisdictions.
  • Develop appropriate and coherent benchmarks and frameworks for personnel roles that are localised, including remuneration, benefits and capacity, and use these to inform organisational planning, monitoring and recruitment.
  • Oversee and manage human resources systems, including employment arrangements in different jurisdictions, benefits, onboarding, performance management and other HR related systems.
  • Ensure human resources practices are compliant with applicable local legislation and organisational policies.
  • Support the enhancement of a wellbeing culture at IDC with related systems and benefits.
  • Oversee and support the Administration Coordinator's implementation of HR processes, ensuring systems are consistent, effective and fit for purpose.

Risk, Compliance and Contracts

  • Work closely with the ED to coordinate the organisational risk management framework, including the development, monitoring and mitigation of key organisational risks.
  • Manage and provide oversight of the organisation's legal entities and ensure statutory, regulatory and governance obligations are met as needed.
  • Establish and maintain appropriate internal controls across financial, operational, HR, data and compliance functions.
  • Oversee the organisation's grant finance compliance infrastructure, working closely with the ED, Programmes Manager and Grants and Finance Officer.
  • Ensure systems are in place to monitor donor financial and administrative requirements, contractual obligations, reporting deadlines and compliance risks.
  • Oversee organisational contracts and agreements, ensuring appropriate systems for review, approval, documentation and record-keeping.
  • Coordinate legal, tax and compliance advice where required.
  • Ensure appropriate continuity, sustainability and contingency planning is in place.

Policies, Systems and Administration

  • Lead the development, review and implementation of organisational policies, procedures and operational frameworks, liaising with the Executive Director.
  • Ensure organisational processes, approval pathways and delegated authorities are clear, proportionate and consistently applied.
  • Provide strategic oversight of IT, cybersecurity, data protection and digital infrastructure.
  • Ensure appropriate systems, security arrangements and technology standards are in place for a global remote organisation.
  • Oversee organisational procurement frameworks and controls.
  • Provide oversight and support to the Administration Coordinator, ensuring administrative systems are efficient and responsive to organisational needs.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve systems and reduce unnecessary administrative burden.

Organisational Development & Operational Improvement

  • Lead the ongoing development of the organisation's operational infrastructure and systems, as its size, funding and geographic reach evolve.
  • Regularly and proactively assess organisational systems, platforms, capacity and processes to identify gaps, risks and opportunities for improvement.
  • Develop practical frameworks and standards to strengthen organisational effectiveness, accountability and resilience.
  • Lead operational improvement and organisational development initiatives and monitor their implementation.
  • Identify emerging organisational needs and advise the ED on appropriate systems, structures and resourcing.
  • Any other relevant tasks agreed with the Executive Director.

Core Responsibilities

  • Actively contribute to a culture of agile learning, collaboration, teamwork and support within IDC’s team.
  • Demonstrate passion and alignment with IDC’s mission, vision and core values of innovation, collaboration, respect, inclusion, representation and being solutions-focused.
  • Demonstrate an understanding of IDC policies to ensure a positive and safe working environment for all.
  • Actively engage with organisational systems, processes and infrastructure to ensure sustainability and appropriate safeguarding of institutional knowledge, assets and core activities over time.

Key Selection Criteria

Essential Criteria

  • Relevant tertiary qualification and/or equivalent professional experience in business administration, finance, human resources, organisational management, non-profit management or a related field.
  • Significant experience in operations, organisational management, finance and/or administration within a non-profit, social impact or other complex organisation.
  • Demonstrated experience managing and supporting personnel responsible for finance, HR, administration or other operational functions.
  • Strong understanding of organisational financial management, including budgeting, forecasting, financial controls and financial risk.
  • Experience overseeing HR and employment processes, ideally across multiple jurisdictions or employment arrangements.
  • Experience managing organisational compliance and/or legal or regulatory requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop, implement and improve organisational systems, policies and processes.
  • Experience working in a geographically distributed or remote organisation or demonstrated ability to manage operational functions across locations.
  • Strong judgement, problem-solving and prioritisation skills, with the ability to balance strategic priorities with responsive day-to-day operational needs.
  • A high level of flexibility and adaptability, including the ability to work well and collaboratively with others.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and practically regarding complex matters.
  • High level of integrity, discretion and attention to detail, with the ability to handle sensitive financial, personnel and organisational matters.

Desirable Criteria

  • Experience operating across multiple jurisdictions
  • Experience with grant management and donor compliance
  • Experience with HR, finance, IT or other organisational systems and technology.
  • Experience in a human rights, migration, social justice or other values-driven organisation.

Application Process

To apply for this role, please upload your resume and a cover letter on IDC Careers’ Webpage, by Tuesday 1st December 2026. Please ensure that you clearly address all of the key selection criteria in your application.

If you have enquiries, please write to . Please note that applications will not be accepted if sent by email.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. The selected candidate will be expected to start as soon as possible.

NB: All applications must be submitted in English.

We envision a world where immigration detention no longer exists. And we work with everyone to make that vision a reality. We believe people should be able to live freely while they await the outcome of their immigration case, and we advocate for the human rights and dignity of everyone impacted by immigration detention.

IDC is solutions-focused, meaning that we work with lived experience leaders, governments, decision-makers, civil society, UN agencies and other actors to deliver alternatives that benefit migrants, communities and society at large. We are truly global, uniting a coalition of civil society organisations, community groups and individuals from all over the world. While the movement spans continents, we all have a clear purpose: to reduce and ultimately end immigration detention and to promote alternatives.

IDC values diversity, equality and inclusivity. Applications are welcome from all backgrounds. We especially encourage applications of those from underrepresented backgrounds, including but not limited to gender, race, age, sexual orientation, disability and religion. In particular, we highly encourage leaders with lived experience of the impacts of detention to apply. If potential candidates require any adaptations to usual recruitment processes, please do not hesitate to note this in your application

Salary: 48,000 - 56,000 EUR Annually

Since 2017, YiYiEnglish has been providing high quality English lessons to students in China. Our goal is to provide an excellent, accessible educational opportunity to our students. If you’re a qualified teacher who has a passion for teaching, you’ve found the perfect place!

Our business practice requires close collaboration with teachers, so you’ll have your own dedicated associate to ask questions to, receive feedback from, and to discuss student related topics.

All of our students subscribe to a regular schedule. This means that our teachers will have a consistent schedule that will be stable throughout your contract with us. Learning matters, it’s important. Educational progress, development, and success are a priority at YiYiEnglish. We genuinely care whether students learn, hone, and master English. We understand the burden of responsibility of introducing young students to English. It’s our collective responsibility to provide our students with a warm, caring, and judgement free learning space so they can develop a love for English. If done properly, the impact that we can make on our student’s lives can be consequential and life changing. If you share our passion for teaching then YiYiEnglish is the perfect place for you!

YiYiEnglish relies on our teachers to exemplify our teaching philosophy. We want teachers who genuinely care about their students. We want teachers who take their work seriously and who can show that they are responsible and passionate teachers.

Senior Product Development Lead - Maternity Cover

About Voice 21

Oracy is our ability to articulate our ideas, develop understanding, and engage with others through speaking, listening and communication. Like reading, writing and maths, oracy is fundamental for learning and life. Every child should be taught how to use their voice to thrive in education and beyond. Voice 21 is the national charity on a mission to secure high quality oracy education for every child. We know that teaching oracy skills improves children’s confidence, wellbeing, engagement and attainment. We support teachers and school leaders to weave oracy into everyday teaching and whole-school culture, to transform learning and outcomes for their pupils. We focus where we can make the most difference, in state schools that serve economically disadvantaged pupils. We also work to influence national policy and champion oracy across the education system. Follow the links to find out moreabout why oracy is so vitaland theimpact Voice 21 has.

About this role

We are developing our training and professional development offer for teachers that has the potential to reach new audiences, meet needs identified in the education system and widen our impact. To do this well, we need someone who can bring together all the moving parts including content, delivery, marketing, tech and evaluation and drive the work forward with focus and pace.

Right now, responsibility for this sits across several teams, so this role will have collaboration at its core, giving us the dedicated capacity and coordination we need to get this right.

Main responsibilities

The Senior Product Development Lead will take over responsibility for the new product, from early development through to pilot and national launch. They will:

  • Lead the planning, timelines and decision‑making
  • Coordinate input from Product, Delivery, Communications, Technology and Learning & Insight
  • Ensure the product is well‑designed, well‑tested and ready for scale
  • Keep the work moving, remove blockers and maintain clear reporting
  • Shape the commercial model and roll‑out plan
  • Use pilot insight to refine the product and strengthen its value

This role will sit with the Director of Programmes to ensure strong alignment with delivery, implementation and organisational priorities.

We are looking for someone who brings:

  • Strong project management experience
  • Experience developing or launching new products or programmes
  • Understanding of commercial models and routes to market, especially in the education sector
  • Confidence working across multiple teams and disciplines
  • Ability to turn ideas into clear plans and deliver them
  • Comfort with ambiguity and a focus on getting things done

What success looks like after 12 months

  • A high‑quality training product developed and tested
  • A clear, evidence‑based recommendation for national roll‑out
  • A well‑designed pilot with strong insight
  • A commercial and operational plan ready for launch
  • Clear ownership and processes for long‑term delivery
  • Strong collaboration across Product, Delivery, Comms, Tech and Insight

Who you’ll work with:This post sits within the Programme Directorate. The line manager for this post is the Director of Programmes, Tim Judge.

Further details

Start date: End of February 2027

Terms: 12 months linked to maternity cover and subject to successful probation review.

Contract: FTE contract

Location: Home-based with frequent national travel, including overnight stays, to work with schools and attend meetings. Applicants must hold a valid UK driving licence and have access to a car they can use for work.

Application details

To apply:

Please submit your most recent CV and a document answering the questions below:

  • Tell us why you want to work at Voice 21. What is it about us and our mission that excites you? (Max. 400 words)
  • Making direct reference to the job description, please tell us the three main reasons why you would make an excellent Senior Product Development Lead (Max. 400 words).
  • Tell us about something you have achieved recently that you are proud of? (Max 200 words)

Closing date: Tuesday 8th December 2026, mid-night

Interview date: Interviews are likely to take place during the week commencing 14th December 2026.

Questions: If you have any questions before applying for the role, please contact Tim Judge at

Valuing every voice

Voice 21 believes that every voice should be heard and valued. We are committed to the equal treatment of all current and prospective employees and do not condone discrimination on the basis of age, disability, sex, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race or ethnicity, religion or belief, gender identity, or marriage and civil partnership.

We aspire to have a diverse and inclusive workplace and strongly encourage suitably qualified applicants from a wide range of backgrounds to apply and join Voice 21.

raw.description:
Location: fully remote

Employment type: Part-time | 16 hours/week | Equity-based

About Bizmoni Corp.

Bizmoni is building an AI Business Network designed to help people and businesses connect, earn, learn, and grow in the AI era.

As a seed-stage, pre-revenue company, we are strengthening our platform, growing our global ecosystem, and laying the foundations for future funding and scale. This is an opportunity to join an entrepreneurial, international team and help shape both the product and the business.

About the Role:

Bizmoni is looking for a hands-on Talent Systems & Recruitment Automation Specialist to review, optimize and automate our recruitment processes using Manatal.

This is not a recruiter position. You will work closely with Talent Acquisition and Operations to understand our recruitment workflow, identify manual work and system gaps, and translate them into practical ATS configuration, automation, integration, and reporting solutions.

Experience with Manatal is preferred but not mandatory. We are also interested in candidates with strong hands-on experience improving other ATS, HRIS, CRM or workflow automation platforms.

What You'll Do:

    • Review our current recruitment workflow and identify process and automation gaps.
    • Configure and continuously improve Manatal workflows, pipelines, fields, templates and reporting.
    • Automate repetitive recruiter activities and administrative tasks.
    • Improve sourcing, screening, interview, candidate tracking and reporting workflows.
    • Build or support integrations between Manatal and other business tools.
    • Work with APIs and automation tools such as Zapier, Make or Power Automate, where appropriate.
    • Create dashboards and reporting that improve visibility into recruiter activity and recruitment performance.
    • Document workflows and train TA users on improved processes.
    • Recommend new automation opportunities as the recruitment function scales.

What You'll Bring:

    • 3+ years of hands-on experience with ATS, HRIS, CRM or recruitment technology systems.
    • Demonstrated experience configuring and improving systems, not simply using them as an end user.
    • Strong understanding of recruitment workflows and Talent Acquisition operations.
    • Experience with workflow automation, APIs, integrations or tools such as Zapier, Make or Power Automate.
    • Experience with Manatal, Greenhouse, Lever, Workable, Ashby or comparable ATS platforms.
    • Ability to identify inefficient processes and translate business requirements into practical system solutions.
    • Strong analytical, documentation, and problem-solving skills.
    • Ability to work independently in a global remote startup environment.

What we expect:

  • Innovative and growth-driven: Proactively pursue opportunities with partners who will enhance our users' experiences
  • Flexible Hours: Meet deadlines and attend meetings in a schedule that suits you
  • Language Proficiency: Fluent in English. Spanish and Portuguese are a plus
  • Remote Discipline: Self-motivated and able to work independently
  • Goal-Oriented Mindset: A proactive, creative problem solver who drives results
  • Required Equipment: Personal computer with a camera and reliable internet
  • Equity-First Compensation: Willingness to accept equity + commission as initial payment until we run the 2nd phase of our investments

Who Thrives at Bizmoni?

We look for people who demonstrate:

  • Ownership – Taking responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks
  • Results Orientation – Focusing on quality, execution, and impact
  • Continuous Improvement – Always looking for better ways to work and improve quality
  • Collaboration – Partnering effectively across teams and functions
  • Adaptability—Thriving in a dynamic and evolving environment
  • Mission Alignment—Believing in what we're building and its future potential

Compensation & Commitment

Bizmoni currently offers ONLY an equity-based compensation model, aligned with global startup practices that enable early contributors to participate in the company's potential long-term value creation.

The role requires a flexible commitment of approximately 16 hours per week, with clear deliverables and results-driven accountability. Contributors may maintain a primary paid role alongside their engagement with Bizmoni. As Bizmoni is currently seed-stage, compensation is provided in company equity. Full terms and conditions will be discussed during the selection process and confirmed in the consulting agreement.

Requirements for Remote Engagement:

  • Personal computer with camera and reliable internet connection.
  • Willingness to participate in Bizmoni's equity-based compensation model.

Why You'll Love Working at Bizmoni

  • Help shape the quality foundation of an emerging AI Business Network
  • Influence products and processes from an early stage
  • Work with a talented and globally distributed team
  • Gain exposure to AI, FinTech, product, and technology initiatives
  • Contribute directly to Bizmoni's readiness for future funding and scale

Equal Opportunity Employer

Bizmoni is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive global environment where everyone is treated with dignity, fairness, and respect.

Engagement decisions are based on relevant skills, experience, potential, and business needs, without discrimination based on any characteristic protected by applicable law. We believe diverse perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences strengthen our culture, innovation, and global network.

Before Applying, Ask Yourself:

  • Are you open to ONLY equity-based compensation?
  • Are you open to dedicating a min. of 16 hrs weekly on our project?

If your answers are YES then we are happy to meet you!

Recruitment Process:

  • Interview with TA Partner.
  • Interview with COS and CEO.
  • Offer (based on final positive feedback).

Please send us your English CV stating the role you apply. Only shortlisted candidates are selected for the interview. Thank you.
